issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may set aside an acquittal when, after considering the trial court’s reasons and reappraising the evidence, it finds those reasons unsustainable.
material_facts: The trial court acquitted the accused after listing thirteen circumstances it considered inconsistent with the prosecution case.
The High Court reappraised the evidence, rejected the trial court’s reasons as unsustainable, and convicted the accused.
The Supreme Court agreed with the High Court’s reasons for setting aside the acquittal.
issues.conclusion: The High Court committed no error in reversing the acquittal, and its judgment disclosed no illegality or infirmity.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal against acquittal under Sections 378(1) and 378(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the appellate court must consider the trial court’s reasons. If two views are possible and the trial court adopted the view favourable to the accused, the acquittal should not be disturbed; the High Court may nevertheless reverse it when its reasons show that the acquittal is unsustainable. The judgment cites no earlier case by name for this principle.

rule.if: appeal_against_acquittal and trial_court_stated_reasons and appellate_court_reappraised_evidence and appellate_review_found_trial_reasons_unsustainable

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The prosecution appealed an acquittal, and the appellate court set it aside.
predicates.trial_court_stated_reasons: The trial court gave reasons for acquitting the accused.
predicates.appellate_court_reappraised_evidence: The appellate court reconsidered the evidence on the record.
predicates.appellate_review_found_trial_reasons_uns: The appellate court identified reasons, on reviewing the evidence, for finding the trial court’s grounds for acquittal unsustainable.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an acquittal and the appellate court reappraises the evidence and finds the trial court’s stated reasons unsustainable, reversal of the acquittal is sustainable.

issues.legal_issue: The testimony of eyewitnesses who are related to the deceased is not to be rejected solely because of that relationship or because independent eyewitnesses were not examined.
material_facts: Several eyewitnesses were close relatives of the deceased.
Their presence at the scene was natural in light of the time and place of the incident.
Their accounts corroborated one another in material particulars, and cross-examination disclosed no material infirmity in the principal account.
The defence argued that the witnesses should not be believed because they were related to the deceased and independent eyewitnesses had not been examined.
issues.conclusion: The eyewitnesses’ evidence could safely be relied upon despite their relationship to the deceased.
issues.legal_principle: Related eyewitness testimony cannot be discarded merely because of the witnesses’ relationship to the deceased. The court must be on guard and scrutinize such testimony closely. The judgment invokes this as a settled principle but names no earlier case or statutory provision for it.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_after_acquittal_reversal and eyewitnesses_are_related_to_deceased and eyewitnesses_were_naturally_present and accounts_are_materially_corroborated and cross_examination_revealed_no_material_infirmity

predicates.criminal_appeal_after_acquittal_reversal: The accused brought a criminal appeal after an appellate court reversed their acquittal.
predicates.eyewitnesses_are_related_to_deceased: The eyewitnesses were close relatives of the deceased.
predicates.eyewitnesses_were_naturally_present: The circumstances of the time and place made the eyewitnesses’ presence at the scene natural.
predicates.accounts_are_materially_corroborated: The eyewitnesses’ accounts supported one another on material particulars.
predicates.cross_examination_revealed_no_material_i: Cross-examination did not reveal a material infirmity in the eyewitnesses’ account.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal follows reversal of an acquittal, related eyewitnesses were naturally present, their accounts corroborate one another materially, and cross-examination reveals no material infirmity, their testimony may be relied on.

issues.legal_issue: Medical evidence that is consistent with the injuries described by eyewitnesses does not discredit their account.
material_facts: The medical evidence and post-mortem reports recorded injuries caused by sharp-edged weapons and by lathis.
The accused argued that the medical evidence did not support the eyewitnesses’ account.
The Supreme Court found no substance in that argument after reviewing the medical evidence and reports.
issues.conclusion: The medical evidence did not undermine the eyewitnesses’ account.
issues.legal_principle: The court assesses medical evidence against the eyewitness account; here, the recorded injuries were consistent with the described use of sharp-edged and blunt weapons. The judgment cites no earlier case or statutory provision for this conclusion.

predicates.criminal_appeal_after_acquittal_reversal: The accused brought a criminal appeal after an appellate court reversed their acquittal.
predicates.medical_evidence_records_injuries_consis: Medical evidence recorded injuries consistent with the weapons and assault described by the eyewitnesses.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal follows reversal of an acquittal and the medical evidence records injuries consistent with the eyewitness account, the medical evidence does not discredit that account.
